comparison: Perfect agreement on IAA treatment methodology (C6, C65-C69, C151-C152). Both evaluations support the finding that IAA enhances detection of sulfur modifications. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewers accept this methodological advance without challenge.

Perfect agreement on methodological limitations (C107-C109, C112). Both acknowledge the gap between predicted and detected modifications and the need for complementary approaches like mass spectrometry. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for acknowledging limitations; peer reviewers also accept these limitations but want them addressed more thoroughly.

Disagreement on mnmA phenotype claims (C8, C99-C104, C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on in vitro and macrophage infection data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting inadequate phenotype analysis and requesting complementation experiments to strengthen the growth defect claims.

Agreement on genetic validation (C7, C73-C75 for MnmA; peer also includes C93-C94 for TruB). Both evaluations support the deletion mutant experiments. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers find the genetic validation 'convincing' and accept these experiments.

Disagreement on mechanistic understanding (C119-C126 in OpenEval overlap with C127-C130, C134 in peer review). OpenEval rates phenotype synthesis as SUPPORTED but mechanistic hypotheses separately as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the mechanistic basis and noting lack of experimental validation for selectivity hypotheses.

Agreement on core tRNA-seq results (C5, C53-C54, C98). Both evaluations support the detection of modifications through tRNA-seq methodology. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers state 'conclusions are mostly supported by the data' though noting limitations in comprehensiveness.

Agreement on chemical treatment validation in E. coli (C76-C82). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for CMC and alkali treatment methods. Peer reviewers accept these chemical treatment findings without challenge, noting they 'enhance reverse transcription signals.'

Disagreement on bioinformatics predictions (C4, C31-C32). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the BLAST homology methodology sound. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting bioinformatic analysis is 'partial' and 'incomplete,' requesting additional phylogenetic analyses and comparison with published mass spec data.

Disagreement on phylogenetic distribution claims (C40, C42, C46-C47, C49-C50). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for distribution patterns in Figure 1. Peer reviewers rate broader bioinformatic claims as UNCERTAIN, requesting strengthening through further analyses.

Disagreement on functional predictions from homology (C33-C36). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding essentiality data properly cited and functional inference reasonable. Peer reviewers rate bioinformatic predictions as UNCERTAIN, noting incompleteness of analysis.

Agreement on chemical treatment application to Mtb (C83-C89). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding RT signatures match E. coli patterns. Peer reviewers accept chemical treatment findings, noting they confirm presence of modifications.

Agreement on Ψ55 validation (C90-C94). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with converging chemical and genetic evidence. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of chemical treatment validation (C90-C91) and genetic validation (C93-C94).

Agreement on Ψ38-39 prediction (C95-C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on enzyme homology and CMC signatures, noting lack of genetic validation. Peer reviewers accept CMC treatment findings without specific challenge to these predictions.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic hypotheses (C127-C135). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting oxidative stress and codon usage hypotheses lack experimental validation. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the mechanistic basis and selectivity explanations.

Agreement on IAA methodological advance (C150-C152). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for expanded utility of IAA treatment. Peer reviewers accept this methodological contribution as part of their evaluation of IAA treatment findings.

Partial overlap on MiaA essentiality (C37-C39). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the differential essentiality pattern reasonable though speculative. Peer reviewers include C38-C39 in their UNCERTAIN rating of bioinformatic predictions, wanting additional validation.
OpenEval identifies unexplained RT signatures (C113-C118) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific unusual signature claims.

OpenEval identifies absence of s2U-modifying enzyme homologs (C136-C139) and rates as SUPPORTED for the gap identification, with speculation about alternative pathways. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval identifies TrmR enzyme-substrate mismatch (C140-C145) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative explanations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific enzyme puzzle.
